question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(t)=6{t}^{6}+15{t}^{5}+6{t}^{4}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(t)=0,$ that is

$$
6{t}^{6}+15{t}^{5}+6{t}^{4}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3{t}^{4}.$ We can factor out the $3{t}^{4}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{4}(2{t}^{2}+5t+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{t}^{2}+5t+2$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{4}(2{t}^{2}+5t+2) & =0 \\ 3{t}^{4}(2t+1)(t+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $t=0,$ $t=-\frac{1}{2},$ and $t=-2.$
